title: Cloud Run: request, container and the scale-to-zero model

videos.script: Cloud Run does not run servers. It runs containers that answer requests, and it starts and stops them as the requests come and go. {{contract}} First, the contract. Your container listens on the port it is given, keeps nothing it needs later, and stops when it is told. Keep those promises, and Google takes care of the address, the certificate and the number of copies. {{build}} Then you build the shop's orders service. Fifty lines of Python and a five-line Dockerfile. {{home}} You run it at home, and break the contract twice on purpose. Once by listening in the wrong place. Once with a command that cannot hear the signal to stop, and costs ten seconds every time. {{zero}} Last, scale to zero. No requests, no instances, no bill. And the first request after a quiet hour pays for the start.
